cluster_summary: This cluster covers authorization vulnerabilities where the application fails to properly validate sender identity, trust boundaries, or access policies. The majority of issues stem from using mutable or partial identifiers for authorization, treating empty allowlists as permissive, missing authorization gates on secondary event types, or incorrectly merging authorization contexts. The cluster also includes a few distinct sub-patterns such as pre-authentication crypto work and stale queued action validation.
guideline_text: Trace mutable files, paths, objects, identities, request fields, or shared state that are checked before use into sensitive file, state, permission, memory, or resource effects that depend on the earlier check. Report code paths where the checked value is not stabilized with a handle, lock, transaction, immutable copy, or atomic operation before the effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 21 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should bind the check to a stable reference or perform the check and effect under the same atomic operation or synchronization boundary.

mechanism.missing_guard: the checked value is not stabilized with a handle, lock, transaction, immutable copy, or atomic operation before the effect
mechanism.name: time-of-check to time-of-use on mutable object
mechanism.sink_shape: sensitive file, state, permission, memory, or resource effects that depend on the earlier check
mechanism.source_shape: mutable files, paths, objects, identities, request fields, or shared state that are checked before use
mechanism.typical_fix: bind the check to a stable reference or perform the check and effect under the same atomic operation or synchronization boundary

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Replace mutable/partial identifiers with immutable unique IDs (e.g., numeric user ID, full MXID, canonical phone number) and normalize inputs before comparison.
sub_patterns.name: Authorization based on mutable or incomplete identifiers
sub_patterns.root_cause: Code used user-controlled mutable attributes (display name, username, room name) or partial identity components instead of immutable unique identifiers, allowing spoofing or impersonation.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Make empty allowlists fail closed: return false when the allowlist is empty. For route-level allowlists, preserve the explicit empty list and do not fall back to wildcard.
sub_patterns.name: Empty allowlist treated as permissive
sub_patterns.root_cause: Authorization functions returned true when the allowlist was empty, assuming an empty list means unrestricted access instead of denying all.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Separate DM and group allowlist composition; exclude pairing-store entries from group checks and use only explicit groupAllowFrom or fallback allowFrom.
sub_patterns.name: Cross-context allowlist contamination (DM/group merge)
sub_patterns.root_cause: DM pairing-store entries were incorrectly included in group allowlist evaluation, allowing DM-approved users to bypass group authorization.

sub_patterns.name: Inadequate sender authorization checks on identity and event handling
